title: Fragmented kernel orchestration for hybrid expert (MoE/GQA/MHA) model onboarding
creator: Diego Rios
description: Problem: New hybrid models (Mixture-of-Experts variants mixed with grouped/query attention and multihead attention layers) show high variance across latency and memory when compiled with a single monolithic profile. We need an orchestration approach that can compile per-fragment kernel artifacts, pin a per-model routing policy, and publish deterministic performance profiles to the model catalog so runtime can select optimized kernels and fall back safely.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model published profile includes: kernel-map, compile-artifact checksum, pinned kernel version, and expected latency/throughput range
Runtime can route fragments to pinned kernels with a transparent fallback to a compatible kernel within 5% latency degradation
CI reproduces compile artifacts from the published profile (checksum match) in >=95% of attempts across supported GPU families
E2E regression tests show no >5% token-latency regression vs baseline for canonical prompts in canary lanes
Observability: telemetry emits per-request kernel decision, compile-profile-id, and a delta to expected latency
implementation_notes: Introduce a compile manifest with fragment identifiers (module:layer-range:type) and allow multiple kernel bindings per fragment prioritized by cost/latency/compatibility
Extend model-onboarder to run a fragment-aware compile pass that outputs a unified profile bundle and publish to model-catalog as immutable artifact (profile-id).
Add a pinning API: model_version -> profile_id, with rollout metadata (canary %), and a rollback TTL to auto-unpin on stale revisions.
Runtime must implement fragment routing hooks: query kernel-map by fragment, attempt primary kernel, on failure pick next compatible kernel and emit event with decision path.
Safety nets: reject profile publish if any fragment compilation fails on all target architectures; provide a soft-fail publish mode for experiments behind flags.
test_plan: Microbench harness: per-fragment latency/throughput sweep across seq-lens [32,128,512] and batch sizes [1,8,32] on target GPUs (A100, H100, V100-equivalent).
Determinism CI: retrieve profile bundle, rebuild compile artifacts inside hermetic builder, verify checksums match published artifacts (run 5 replicates).
Canary: roll profile to 5% of requests for 48h with active monitoring of p50/p95 token latency and error rates; compare to control route.
Regression tests: run canonical prompts for translation/summarization/chat and ensure output-equivalence score within acceptable thresholds when using fallback kernels.
Chaos: simulate kernel OOM/driver failure and ensure runtime selects fallback kernel without request-level data exposure and with clear telemetry.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Internal: publish profile to catalog as staged, run internal perf smoke and determinism tests.
Stage 1 - Canary: pin profile to model_version with 5% traffic split for 48h; monitor metrics and abort on SLA breaches.
Stage 2 - Ramp: increase to 25% then 75%, observe for 24h windows and validate cost/latency targets.
Stage 3 - General availability: promote profile to default pinned profile for the model_version and mark older profile as archived.
Rollback: immediate unpin and revert to last-good profile if p95 latency or error rate exceed thresholds for >15 minutes.
